title: What does LoanBrokerCoverDeposit do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LoanBrokerCoverDeposit and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LoanBrokerCoverDeposit adds first-loss capital to a loan broker's cover balance. [1]

Cover supports the broker's lending arrangement and is accounted separately from an individual borrower payment. Depositing it does not itself originate a loan or eliminate credit risk. Confirm which asset and broker receive the contribution. Review the applicable withdrawal and loss rules before describing the amount as freely available liquidity. [1]

The LoanBrokerCoverDeposit reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LoanBrokerCoverDeposit, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
